fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

`decksite/testutil.py`'s `with_test_db()` decorator called `database.setup()` for every decorated test, which iterates all 76 migration files one by one — slow (~5.5 s on a developer laptop per the issue reporter).

## What changed

- Added `decksite/schema.sql`: a dump of the database schema **plus seed data** (source names, archetypes, competition types, seasons, etc.) generated from a fresh migration run (`mysqldump --no-tablespaces --skip-comments decksite_schema_gen`, with the MariaDB 11.8 sandbox-mode directive stripped for portability). The file is 704 lines.
- Modified `decksite/testutil.py` `with_test_db()` to read `schema.sql` and execute its statements directly, replacing the `database.setup()` call. The `from decksite import database` import (only needed for `database.setup()`) was also removed.

When new migrations are added, `schema.sql` must be regenerated by running `mysqldump --no-tablespaces --skip-comments <decksite_db> > decksite/schema.sql` against a freshly migrated database and committing the result.

## How it was validated

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed on all touched files.
- `uv run --frozen python -m pytest decksite/ --ignore=decksite/scrapers -m 'not functional and not perf'` — 425 passed, 5 deselected. This includes `test_equivalent_names_are_stored_and_found_as_one_identity`, the only test decorated with `@with_test_db`, which exercises the full schema-load path including seed-data lookup (`source` table → 'League').

Fixes #8433
fix.pr_title: Load test DB from schema.sql instead of running all migrations (#8433)
